Sales Basics in Malayalam (course)

10 short video lessons (about 70–90 seconds each in the current version) for students, freshers and job seekers with no sales experience. Lessons: 1 What sales really is · 2 The seller's mindset · 3 Features vs benefits · 4 Know your customer · 5 The first 30 seconds · 6 Ask, then listen · 7 Present the value · 8 Handling objections · 9 Close with a next step · 10 Your first real sale. Includes worksheets, a 10-question quiz (pass 7/10) and a certificate. Price: shared on WhatsApp +91 99958 42727. It leads to the practical session and the Accent Sales Program.
Lesson 1 · What sales really is

Sales is understanding a person's problem and giving the right solution, not pushing. Trust is the real product. Everyone already sells daily (permission at home, friends, interviews). Sales is a career: telecaller, business development, field sales, retail, real estate, insurance. Every sale has 5 steps: Open, Ask, Present, Handle objections, Close. Task: spot one sale today and note how it started and ended.
Lesson 2 · The seller's mindset

A "no" is not about you: not needed now, wrong time, or the need wasn't understood. Every no is a lesson. Help, don't push: ask yourself "how can I help them?". Never lie or invent features; honest sales bring referrals. Sales is a habit: track calls, conversations and sales daily; judge the week, not the day. Task: recall one no and write its real reason.
Lesson 3 · Features vs benefits

Feature = what the product has. Benefit = what it does for the customer. People buy benefits. The "So what?" test turns a feature into a benefit (50 km mileage → less money on petrol). Different people care about different benefits (student: camera; shop owner: battery). Task: 5 features → 5 benefits on the worksheet.
Lesson 4 · Know your customer

Know every customer in 4 boxes: Need, Budget, Decider, Timing. Talk to the person who pays and decides. Ask the budget politely ("roughly how much are you looking at?"). In Kerala families often decide together: ask if anyone else should be part of it and fix a time with them. Task: fill the 4 boxes for someone's recent purchase.
Lesson 5 · The first 30 seconds

Opening formula: Greet · Name · Reason · Permission ("can we talk for 2 minutes?"). Smile on the phone. At a door or shop: clean clothes, ID card visible, one step back, wait if the owner is busy, and ask for a time if they are busy. Avoid: product before your name, starting with "are you busy?", rushing. Task: write and record a 30-second opening.
Lesson 6 · Ask, then listen

Questions come first, like a doctor checking before medicine. Closed questions get yes/no; open questions get people talking. 5 questions: How do you do it now? What's hardest? What changes if it's fixed? Who decides? When do you need it? Don't interrupt, wait a second after they stop, then repeat back what you heard. Task: ask someone at home the 5 questions.
Lesson 7 · Present the value

Don't dump every feature. Use the bridge: You said (their problem) → So this (one matching feature) → Which means (their benefit). Max 3 points. Show rather than tell (demo, photo). Never use fake numbers or reviews. After each point ask "will this help you?". Task: write 3 bridges.
Lesson 8 · Handling objections

Common objections: too costly, I'll think about it, not interested. They signal a doubt, not failure. Method: Listen · Agree · Ask · Answer, never argue. Too costly: don't cut the price, ask what amount they had in mind, compare with the cost of their problem; mention a fee reduction only if one really exists (never say "offer"). I'll think: ask what is left to think about. Not interested: ask why, then thank them and leave. No false promises, no "today only" pressure.
Lesson 9 · Close with a next step

A talk without a close is just a class. Summarise in one line, ask clearly ("shall we start?"), then stay quiet. If yes: confirm what, when, who on WhatsApp. If not now: fix an exact callback time and ask for feedback on the talk. Call exactly on time. Task: record a full mock call.
Lesson 10 · Your first real sale

Videos alone don't teach selling, like swimming. Practical session: Step 1 online role-play lab, Step 2 offline workshop with a trainer, Step 3 a real field task in local shops. Complete all three for the Field Ready certificate. Top learners get a priority interview for the Accent Sales Program. Book via WhatsApp +91 99958 42727.
Practical sessions

P1 Online role-play lab: 2 hours on Google Meet, 10–12 learners. P2 Offline sales workshop: 3 hours in Manjeri, 15–20 learners, 2 trainers. P3 Door-to-door field task: half day in pairs at local shops, trainer support, only real products Accent has permission to promote, no cash collected. Safety: always in pairs, daytime only (10:00–13:00), shops first, homes only with a trainer nearby, Accent ID card, never enter a home, a no is final, under-18s need written parental consent. Field Ready = rubric average 2.5+ with no 1 in honesty. Dates and fees: shared on WhatsApp.
